analyzed_vuln.description: The LWPOLYLINE `FIELD_2DD_VECTOR` decoder can reach the end of its object/input bit chain while iterating attacker-controlled `num_points`. Although `bit_read_BB_noadv` and `bit_read_DD` have logical bounds checks, `FIELD_DD` first expands `TRACE_DD`, which unconditionally executes `dat->chain[dat->byte]` without checking `dat->byte < dat->size` (dec_macros.h:608-628). At EOF this causes the reported one-byte heap-buffer-overflow before the guarded DD reader can reject the truncated coordinate. The vector precheck is also too permissive at the boundary because `AVAIL_BITS` adds a 20-bit allowance, so it does not guarantee that every encoded point is present.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: A binary DWG (the PoV identifies as AC1015/R2000) must contain an LWPOLYLINE object whose decoded `num_points` causes `FIELD_2DD_VECTOR(points, num_points, 10)` to continue into truncated point data. The object is accepted and the first point is decoded; during a later delta-coordinate iteration the bit cursor reaches the end of the backing fuzz input (`dat->byte == dat->size`). `bit_read_BB_noadv` reports/returns an error-like value without advancing, then `FIELD_DD` invokes the unguarded `TRACE_DD` byte read at exactly one byte past the heap allocation.
